chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt, who said: I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him):
He said: 'It is the Word of Allah; do not exceed it, and do not seek guidance in other than it, otherwise you will go astray.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of the Qur'an as a source of guidance according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this narration from *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Rida (AS) defines the Qur'an as the uncreated Speech of Allah, establishing it as the exclusive and sufficient source of guidance. He warns against seeking direction in any other medium, thereby affirming the Qur'an's self-sufficiency (*kifayah*) and guarding against the deviation that arises from relying on external or secondary sources.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. Ja`far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (RA) said: Muhammad ibn `Abd Allah ibn Ja`far alHimyari said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of Al-Rayyan ibn al-Salt that I asked al-Rida (AS): “What do you say about the Qur’an?”
Thus, he (AS) responded. “It is the Word of Allah, do not exceed it, and do not seek guidance in other than it, otherwise you will go astray.”
